Q: How to automatically add longer space in Word or LibreOffice? A:

That's not why we used to use two spaces after a period. That was done because they used monospaced fonts, and it aided readability. Every current stylebook says not to do that. You can use "justify" in your paragraph style to get equal word spacing. That's the other alternative to "left", "center", and "right".

Q: How to remove null values generated by a jackson custom serializer? A:

This needs two things now. The member needs to have the annotation @JsonInclude(NON_EMPTY) and the serializer needs to implement:

public boolean isEmpty(
      final SerializerProvider provider,
      final List<String> value)

Q: nginx: unknown directive "redis_pass" in /etc/nginx/common/redis.conf A:

The following error message from nginx

unknown directive "redis_pass"

means that the ngx_http_redis is not installed or not loaded (main part of the nginx.conf is missing).

Q: What is the best way to remember which function to use for which situation? A:

Think about how you would learn chords of a particular song on guitar. How would you do it?

You'd find a guitar tab reference, and study it.

Then you'd play it, probably not the whole song at first, but trying it out in small pieces slowly until you learned the sequence of chords.

Then you'd practice the song, over and over, until it became something you could play from memory.

It's the same with code functions in SQL or Python or any other language.

First you read the reference documentation to see the name and arguments. You study any notes about usage or options.

Then you try the function in a throwaway test or a sandbox if the language supports it.

Finally you carefully try the function in your real code project. You test thoroughly to make sure it works the way you expect.

Eventually you are confident in your understanding and you can use that function easily.

Repeat these steps for every function you use.

If you don't use the function for a few months, you may have to refresh your memory with more reading and testing. That's normal. Everyone does that.

This is undoubtedly the same process of learning that applies to every professional skill.

Study, practice, repeat.

It may not be quick, but it's the best way to remember, which is what you asked.
